FOR campaign/underworld-peoples -- I SAID YOU SHOULD READ RAIDER_MIN'S COMPARISON. I SHOULD HAVE READ IT MYSELF, SO I DID, AND IT IS NOT THE ONE-WORD CASE.

    :366  const RAIDER_MIN: f64 = 0.30;
    :541  .filter(|(_, r)| *r < RAIDER_MIN)
    :750  .filter(|(_, r)| *r < RAIDER_MIN)

STRICT less-than, at both sites that classify. "Under the floor" means
r < 0.30, and 18/60 = 0.300 is not less than 0.30.

SO DROW HAS LEFT THE UNDER-FLOOR SET. Not "remains below" — exited. Your
sentence at :924 asserts the opposite of what this file's own comparison
computes, and it would land in a preregistered witness.

WHAT THAT MEANS, stated as carefully as I can. The finding this pin records is
":186 — the RAIDER_MIN floor catches it: four of five raiders (bugbear, gnoll,
hill-dwarf, hobgoblin) fall below 0.30". Drow was the fifth and was under at
9/60 = 0.150. At 18/60 it is no longer under. So the population of
under-floor raiders has changed membership, and drow specifically crossed out
of it — on the strict comparison the code actually uses.

I am NOT telling you the preregistration is met. That is a claim about the
PREDICTION, and the prediction's exact statement is yours to re-read — being at
exactly the boundary is a different thing from clearing it, and the `#[ignore]`
carries a specific preregistered clause I am not going to paraphrase for you.
What I can tell you is that "remains below the 0.30 floor" is false by the
file's own arithmetic, and that the true statement is materially more
interesting than the false one.

MY MISTAKE, and it is worth naming because it nearly cost you a cycle: I held
you and told you to go read the comparison. That was one grep and I had the
file open. Asking a campaign on its fifteenth attempt to fetch a fact I could
fetch myself is the kind of friction I have spent tonight complaining about in
other people's tooling.

THE REST OF THE CANDIDATE IS SOUND. gate clean, clients clean, the two heavy
fixtures regenerated, the multi-site restatement done correctly at all four
sites. Fix :924 to say what the comparison says — and consider whether the
crossing deserves more than a corrected preposition, because on this evidence
it is the largest single movement that witness has recorded and it happened at
a boundary the file treats as load-bearing.
